error_modes.label: Touch down point control - FLAPS LDG / FLAPS T-O / AOA
error_modes.source: specific:TOUCH DOWN POINT (feet from the beginning of the RWY) [a/ FLAPS LDG - FLAPS T/O - AOA]

texts.0: SP, due to a shallow final flown well beyond the briefed aim point, did not place the touch down point within the required distance from the beginning of the runway, with the result of contact beyond 1500 ft from the threshold. SP carried approach power into the round out and held the aircraft off in a prolonged float without any glidepath correction. IP directed the go-around and took the aircraft for the following landing.
texts.1: SP, due to a flare started late and with excess energy, did not arrest the float over the touchdown zone, with the result that the touch down point reached the 1500 ft limit from the beginning of the runway. SP adjusted aim point and power only after repeated verbal prompting from IP on final and in the flare. The landing stayed inside the tolerance but with no margin remaining.
texts.2: SP, due to an aim point set long on final, did not keep the touch down point inside 1000 ft from the beginning of the runway, with the result of contact at about 1250 ft from the threshold. SP recognized the long trend during the round out, reduced power promptly and completed the landing with no IP input.
texts.3: SP flew a stabilized final on the briefed aim point and touched down within 1000 ft of the beginning of the runway on each landing. Power reduction and flare timing were accurate, so the float was short and predictable. No prompting was required at any point of the approach.
texts.4: SP placed the touch down point within a few aircraft lengths of the briefed aim point on every landing, well inside 1000 ft from the beginning of the runway. Glidepath, power and flare timing were matched so that the landing distance was repeatable from pass to pass.
texts.marginal: SP touched down inside 1000 ft from the beginning of the runway, but consistently in the far part of that band and long of the briefed aim point. The trend comes from a flare begun slightly early followed by a float that is allowed to run. SP is expected to tighten aim point selection and power reduction so that the touch down point is centered in the touchdown zone.

texts_at.0: With the IP flying the approach and calling the aim point and the power reduction, SP followed on the controls through the round out and began comparing the sight picture with the briefed aim point. Selecting the aim point and adjusting power to place the touch down point without prompting have not yet been asked of SP at this stage. The Training Section introduces this maneuver at this point and does not yet ask for an independent standard. SP is expected to begin naming the trend toward long or short on final before adjusting the aim point independently.
texts_at.1: SP kept the touch down point inside the tolerance required at this stage, contacting about 1480 feet from the beginning of the runway. The margin traces to an aim point held on the far side of the touchdown zone rather than adjusted once the approach was stabilized. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to move the aim point closer once the approach is stable so the touch down point sits with more margin under the 1500 foot limit.
texts_at.2: SP kept the touch down point inside the tolerance required at this stage, contacting about 1250 feet from the beginning of the runway. The margin traces to a flare begun a fraction early, letting the float carry the aircraft further down the touchdown zone. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to begin the flare at the briefed height so the float narrows and the touch down point moves closer to the aim point.
texts_at.3: SP touched down about 850 feet from the beginning of the runway, the small margin tracing to power being reduced a moment later than the briefed point short of the aim point. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to reduce power at the briefed point so the touch down point sits still closer to the aim point.

texts_above.1: SP flew a stabilized final on the briefed aim point and touched down about 1450 feet from the beginning of the runway, the aim point adjustment following a verbal call from the IP. This is above the level the Training Section requires at this point.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the long trend during the round out and reduced power promptly, bringing the touch down point back to about 1250 feet from the beginning of the runway without prompting. Reducing power at the briefed point rather than a moment later would tighten that value further. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to sound touchdown point control.
texts_above.3: SP flew a stabilized final on the briefed aim point and touched down about 850 feet from the beginning of the runway, with power reduction and flare timing accurate enough that no correction was needed. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to sure-handed touchdown point control.
texts_above.4: SP placed the touch down point within a few aircraft lengths of the briefed aim point, about 350 feet from the beginning of the runway, with glidepath, power and flare timing matched so the distance was repeatable pass to pass. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to exceptional touchdown point control.

error_modes.label: Centerline tracking at touchdown - FLAPS LDG / FLAPS T-O / AOA
error_modes.source: specific:DEVIATION FROM CENTER LINE (feet) [a/ FLAPS LDG - FLAPS T/O - AOA]

texts.0: SP, due to a drift carried uncorrected through the round out, did not track the runway centerline, with the result of a lateral deviation beyond 15 ft at touchdown that continued to increase during the landing roll. SP applied neither the wing-low correction nor the rudder alignment before contact. IP took the controls to recenter the aircraft on the runway.
texts.1: SP, due to a lateral correction applied only inside the flare, did not hold the runway centerline, with the result of a deviation of about 15 ft at touchdown. SP started recentering the aircraft only after IP called the displacement twice during the landing roll. The deviation stopped at the limit of the tolerance.
texts.2: SP, due to a small lateral offset left uncorrected after the rollout from the final turn, did not keep the deviation from the centerline within 5 ft, with the result of a displacement of about 10 ft at touchdown. SP identified the offset during the round out, applied rudder and aileron and returned to the centerline during the landing roll without assistance.
texts.3: SP tracked the runway centerline through final, flare and landing roll, keeping the deviation within 5 ft. Alignment was maintained with small continuous corrections rather than late large inputs.
texts.4: SP touched down with the main wheels on the runway centerline and a deviation barely perceptible from the cockpit, and held the aircraft aligned for the full landing roll. Directional control was achieved with minimal and precise rudder inputs.
texts.marginal: SP kept the deviation from the centerline within 5 ft, but repeatedly on the same side of the runway and with the correction made late in the flare. The pattern is a fixed lateral offset carried down final rather than active alignment. SP is expected to establish centerline tracking earlier on final so that the touchdown position is not left to the flare.

texts_at.0: With the IP correcting for drift into the flare and calling the alignment, SP followed on the rudder and aileron while beginning to watch the runway edges for lateral movement. Recognizing a developing drift and applying the wing-low correction without prompting have not yet been asked of SP. This is the level of assistance the Training Section still provides at this stage. SP is expected to begin naming any drift observed on short final before correcting it independently.
texts_at.1: SP held the deviation from the runway centerline inside the tolerance required at this stage, touching down about 14 feet off centerline. The margin traces to the lateral correction being applied inside the flare rather than established earlier on final. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to correct any drift on final, before the flare, so the touchdown deviation narrows.
texts_at.2: SP held the deviation from the runway centerline inside the tolerance required at this stage, touching down about 10 feet off centerline. The margin traces to a small lateral offset left uncorrected after the rollout from the final turn. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to correct any offset immediately after rollout so the touchdown deviation narrows further.
texts_at.3: SP touched down about 4 feet off the runway centerline, the small deviation tracing to a late rudder input during the round out rather than continuous alignment through it. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to hold continuous alignment through the round out so this small deviation is removed.

texts_above.1: SP tracked the runway centerline through final and the flare, touching down about 13 feet off centerline after a verbal call from the IP. The result is above the code required for this Training Section at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP identified the lateral offset during the round out, applied rudder and aileron and returned to the centerline during the landing roll, touching down about 10 feet off centerline without assistance. Correcting the offset immediately after rollout, rather than during the round out, would tighten that value further. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to solid centerline tracking at touchdown.
texts_above.3: SP tracked the runway centerline through final, flare and landing roll with small continuous corrections, touching down about 4 feet off centerline rather than with a late large input. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to well-developed centerline tracking at touchdown.
texts_above.4: SP touched down with the main wheels on the runway centerline, deviation barely perceptible at about a foot, and held the aircraft aligned for the full landing roll with minimal and precise rudder inputs. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to outstanding centerline tracking at touchdown.

SP retarded the power lever only after IP called the airspeed on short final. The touchdown remained inside the limit but the float consumed most of the touchdown zone.
texts.2: SP, due to a delayed cross-check of airspeed after the landing configuration change, did not hold the touch down speed within 5 kt of the computed value, with the result of contact about 7 kt fast. SP recognized the excess energy in the round out, reduced power in time and landed without IP intervention.
texts.3: SP flew the final at the computed airspeed and touched down between the computed speed and 5 kt above it. The airspeed cross-check was maintained through the round out and the power reduction was timed to the flare.
texts.4: SP reached the touchdown attitude with the airspeed essentially at the computed value on each landing, with no float and no late power correction. Energy management from the final turn to touchdown was consistent and needed no adjustment.
texts.marginal: SP touched down inside the speed tolerance, but always in the upper part of the band and after a noticeable float. The trend comes from a power reduction started later than the round out. SP is expected to sequence the power reduction with the flare so that the touch down speed sits closer to the computed value.

texts_at.0: With the IP calling the airspeed through the round out and the flare, SP followed on the throttle while beginning to include the airspeed indicator in the scan approaching the flare. Cross-checking airspeed through the round out and matching power to the computed touchdown speed without a reminder have not yet been asked of SP. Performance is consistent with a first exposure at this point of the syllabus, where the Training Section still provides assistance. SP is expected to begin cross-checking airspeed into the flare before holding the computed speed unaided.
texts_at.1: SP held touch down speed inside the tolerance required at this stage, contacting about 9 knots above the computed touchdown speed. The margin traces to an interrupted airspeed cross-check while attention stayed on the aim point through the flare. Performance met the desired standard for this stage. SP is expected to keep airspeed in the cross-check through the flare so the margin above the computed speed narrows.
texts_at.2: SP held touch down speed inside the tolerance required at this stage, contacting about 7 knots above the computed value. The margin traces to a delayed cross-check of airspeed after the landing configuration change. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to cross-check airspeed immediately after configuring so the margin narrows further.
texts_at.3: SP touched down about 3 knots above the computed speed, the small margin tracing to the power reduction being timed a beat after the round out rather than with it. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to time the power reduction with the round out so the margin narrows to the computed value.

texts_above.1: SP flew the final at the computed airspeed and touched down about 8 knots above the computed value, the power retard following a verbal call from the IP. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage of training.
texts_above.2: SP recognized the excess energy in the round out and reduced power in time, touching down about 7 knots fast without IP intervention. Cross-checking airspeed immediately after configuring, rather than a moment later, would tighten that margin further. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to steady touchdown speed control.
texts_above.3: SP flew the final at the computed airspeed and touched down about 3 knots above it, the airspeed cross-check maintained through the round out with the power reduction timed to the flare. This is beyond what the Training Section asks for at this stage, due to consistently accurate touchdown speed control.
texts_above.4: SP reached the touchdown attitude with the airspeed essentially at the computed value, excess of only a knot or so, with no float and no late power correction on any landing. Performance was above the level required at this point of the syllabus, due to exemplary touchdown speed control.

error_modes.label: Round out and float control technique

texts.0: SP, due to a round out initiated high above the runway followed by a released back pressure, did not establish and hold the landing attitude, with the result of a ballooned flare and a hard contact that required an IP recovery. The aircraft was allowed to settle from height with power at idle and no attitude correction. IP took the controls and flew the following pattern as a demonstration.
texts.1: SP, due to a flare rate not matched to the sink rate, did not hold a constant landing attitude through the round out, with the result of two distinct pitch corrections before contact and a touchdown at the edge of the accepted tolerances. SP stabilized the attitude only after IP called for back pressure in the flare. The technique corrected but the touchdown remained firm.
texts.2: SP, due to back pressure applied slightly early in the round out, did not maintain the intended flare profile, with the result of a short balloon before the aircraft settled onto the runway inside the tolerances. SP recognized the balloon at once, held the attitude with a small power addition and completed the landing without IP intervention.
texts.3: SP began the round out at the correct height, held the landing attitude with a smooth increase of back pressure and touched down on the main wheels in the correct attitude. Float was short and controlled and the pitch attitude was held after touchdown.
texts.4: SP flew each round out with the flare rate matched to the sink rate, producing consistent touchdowns on the main wheels with no balloon and no discernible float. Aerodynamic braking after touchdown was held at the correct attitude without prompting.
texts.marginal: SP flew acceptable round outs, but with a flare that varies in height between patterns and a float that runs longer than briefed. The trend suggests judgment of height above the runway that is still developing rather than a control problem. SP is expected to standardize the round out height so the flare produces the same result on each pattern.

texts_at.0: With the IP calling the round out height and the rate of the flare, SP followed on the controls through two round outs and needed the height called on both of them. SP is expected to standardize the round out height so the flare rate needs fewer corrections.
texts_at.2: SP flew the round out and flare inside the standard required at this stage, with a short balloon appearing on one pattern before the aircraft settled inside tolerances. The trend traces to back pressure applied a fraction early in the round out relative to the height available. This is consistent with the expected proficiency for the Training Section. SP is expected to begin back pressure a beat later in the round out so the balloon does not develop.
texts_at.3: SP began the round out at the correct height and touched down on the main wheels in the correct attitude, with only a brief float that judgment of the round out height is still refining. The maneuver was flown to the standard the Training Section requires at this point. SP is expected to hold the same round out height on every pattern so the float shortens further.

texts_above.2: SP recognized the balloon at once and held the attitude with a small power addition, completing the landing without IP intervention on a pattern that started with back pressure a fraction early. Beginning back pressure a beat later in the round out would prevent the balloon from developing at all. The result is above the code required for this Training Section, due to good round out and flare technique.
